_readme: User-visible changes in the replacement app, newest first.

entries.summary: Function-word cards: the active pattern uses the same fill-and-left-bar marker as other senses
detail: The selected pattern box on function-word backs (de, que, em...) now has a 0.24 fill and a 4px left bar in its partner's colour instead of a 2px outline.

entries.summary: Card back: the active sense is marked by a stronger fill and a left bar instead of an outline
detail: The active sense row (and the active sub-meaning inside a grouped sense) now has a 0.24 fill and a 4px bar on its left edge in its word type's colour; the 2px outline is gone.
Applies to single rows, grouped rows, and the group that is lit when several word types are on the card; dark and light theme.
Inactive rows and the word-type rows are unchanged.

entries.summary: 'Level' in the same lighter grey as 'Words 1–100'; level chevrons tight to the number
detail: 'Level' label uses the same brighter grey as the word range.
‹ › buttons are narrower (38px phones, 44px wide desktop; same tap height) with no gap, so they sit beside the number's plate.

entries.summary: Quieter selected level tile; the Level / Words readout a touch more prominent
detail: Selected tile: softer red outline and a faint tint instead of a full red outline and fill.
Level readout: number about 12% larger; 'Level' and 'Words 1–100' one size up, in brighter grey.

entries.summary: Phones show at most 6 level tiles (desktop keeps 8)
detail: Below 1024px the level tile row holds at most 6 tiles, sliding to keep the selected level in view; each tile is about 52px wide instead of 38px.

entries.summary: Example sentences: the pronoun in a pronominal verb (se abre) now takes the verb colour
detail: The reflexive pronoun inside the highlighted verb in an example sentence was orange and underlined; it now uses the same colour as the verb, so 'se abre' reads as one unit.
Sense rows, 'used with' text and chips are unchanged.

entries.summary: Level arrows back beside the level number (phone and desktop), not on the tile row
detail: With level tiles showing, the ‹ › arrows stay beside 'Level N' — the bigger, easier target — instead of moving to the ends of the tile row.
Phone: the tile row has the full width, so tiles are 38px instead of 33px.
Desktop (1360px+): the level column is as wide as the stepper needs, so › no longer crowds the example words.

entries.summary: Desktop home polish: icons beside the titles, ? in the corner, no divider lines, level without its plate
detail: Desktop (1360px+): the leaf and clock icons sit beside 'Learn' and 'Practise'; the ? moves to each column's top-right corner.
Desktop (1360px+): the lines under the titles, above the buttons and above Practise's rows are gone; the shaded plate behind the level number is gone.
Desktop (1360px+): the example words, coverage line and progress bar get a wider share of the row and are centred.
Practise hint (everywhere): 'Mistakes first, then due words' is now 'Mistakes first, then words to review'.

entries.summary: Tutorial updated for phone and desktop: current Smart Skip switch, Conjugate button, right grading and switching instructions per device
detail: Desktop: the note column scrolls to the note being read, so the last notes (Grade your answer) no longer fall off a laptop screen; columns keep one width.
Grading: phones say swipe; computers say Enter / X and point to the keyboard button on the left. Keyboard tips no longer appear on phones.
Speech or music: desktop says Vocabulary in the sidebar; phones say tap the language at the top, then Vocabulary.
Smart Skip page shows the current row with its switch (not Off/On + Details).
Verb cards in the tutorial and walkthrough show the Conjugate button, with a note.
Rare uses: wording mentions the speech-bubble example button; the demo opens a group and shows one example.
Music note says Coming soon in languages without Music.

entries.summary: Desktop home fills the screen without boxes; clearer Practise wording for first-time users
detail: Desktop (1360px+): Learn and Practise are two full-height columns beside the sidebar, split by one line (Practise on a slightly darker ground); title on top, content centred, buttons at the bottom; bigger level number.
Practise, nothing answered yet: 'Nothing to practise yet — When you miss a word, it comes back here. Words you get right come back too, a few days later, so they stick.' (was 'All caught up').
Practise row 'Due for review' is now 'Time to review'.

entries.summary: #/about is a full-screen page again, and shareable: signed-out visitors no longer get sent to sign-in
detail: Opening #/about while signed out shows the About page and never starts sign-in (it used to redirect straight to the sign-in screen).
Signed out: no 'Back to app' button, no sign-in buttons, Escape does nothing — About is the whole page.
About always covers the whole window, sidebar included, signed in or not.

entries.summary: Desktop home uses the window's height; bigger tool buttons on the card back
detail: Desktop (1360px+): Learn and Practise are at least 70% of the window tall (max 720px); tiles at the top, the level with its words and bar centred, Learn button at the bottom.
Card back tool row (Rare uses, Dictionary, …): icons 28→32px and labels 12→14px on phones; 36px and 16px on desktop.

entries.summary: Home: level tiles once you've started two levels; desktop Learn/Practise start at the top; About in the sidebar; dictionary logos fill their circles
detail: Learn: after you've started two levels, a row of tiles (levels started + the next one, up to 8, sliding) with a mini progress bar each replaces the ‹ › stepper arrows. One level started: unchanged stepper.
Desktop (1360px+): Learn keeps the level beside its examples and progress; the Learn/Practise pair is capped at 1140px and starts near the top instead of being centred in the window.
Desktop sidebar: new About item opens the About page.
Card back: the site logos in the Dictionary sheet fill their circle instead of sitting inside it.

entries.summary: Phone top bar: bigger flag and icons, tighter spacing; folded Practise shows only the number waiting
detail: Phone top bar: flag 20→25px, icons 22→26px, language name 15→16px, with the icons closer together.
Folded Practise card: just 'N waiting'; the mistakes / due breakdown no longer appears under it.

entries.summary: Coverage line now for Spanish, Portuguese, French, Finnish; phone top bar and card outline tidied
detail: Coverage shares added for es, pt, fi (OpenSubtitles 2018 lists) and fr (Lexique 4 FreqOrtho), so 'Levels 1–2 make up N% of speech' shows for them. The French deck is only 200 words today.
Phone: the coverage line is back, on its own line under the example words, kept to one line.
Phone top bar: equal space above and below the name and icons; the line beneath is the language's light colour, not the two-colour gradient.
Phone: the open Learn/Practise card has an even outline all the way round (it was thicker on the left).

entries.summary: Level picker: bigger arrows and level number on a shaded plate (trial); coverage line properly hidden on phones
detail: Level picker: the level number is ~25% larger and sits on a shaded rounded plate, with larger arrows either side, so the level reads as the focus of the Learn card.
Fix: the coverage line ('Levels 1–2 make up …') was still showing on phones; it is now desktop-only as intended.

entries.summary: Level picker: 'Levels 1–2 make up 52% of speech' under the example words (desktop)
detail: Speech: shows what the levels up to this one make up of speech, as a whole number, e.g. 'Levels 1–3 make up 57% of speech'. Only languages that ship coverage shares show it (Czech today).
Artist Mode: same wording, 'make up 61% of lyric words', replacing '~61% lyrics comprehension'.
On its own line under the examples; hidden on phones.

entries.summary: Smart Skip row is now the same height as the Learn/Practise button
detail: Smart Skip row: 56px on phones and 62px from 1024px wide, matching the button beside it (it was 54px and 60px).

entries.summary: Level page type tidied; Learn/Practise button text centred in its own half; Portuguese fits the phone language picker
detail: Learn/Practise card: title, level number, 'Level' and 'Words' lines now use one type scale derived from the page text size, with the emphasis font for the title and number; 'Words 101–200' no longer wraps.
Learn / Practise button: the label is centred in the half beside the time chip, not across the whole button (phones and wide screens).
Language picker: a name too long for its tile (Portuguese on a phone) shrinks to fit on one line.

entries.summary: Card back (trial): 'often + a' aligned and set apart; no blank rows; word-type row measured after the flip
detail: llegar: 'to come to · often + a' — the cue sits on the text's baseline, 'often' muted, with ' · ' before a cue that has a word in it (a bare '+ em' stays attached).
In a group the cue follows each translation; when every sub-row has the same cue it is shown once on the shared line ('to reach a place · often + a').
cuerpo: a row is never left blank — when its translation went up to the word-type row, its label ('anatomy') stays on the row as muted context instead of moving into the note.
The word-type row and stacked rows are measured by layout size, not the on-screen box, which the card's 3D flip distorted (cuerpo's 'body' had dropped under the pill).

entries.summary: Card back: quieter word-type pills, aligned 'from caro'; companion cards say '76% of uses of a'
detail: Word-type pills are 14px and tinted (16% fill, coloured text) instead of a solid fill at 19px.
'from caro' matches the pill's size and baseline: 'from' muted, the lemma in the word type's colour.
Companion card fronts read 'Card 1 of 2 · 76% of uses of a', with the word in bold.

entries.summary: Card back (trial): light wash on the open word type and active meaning; ' · ' between translation and context
detail: The active word type's row and the active meaning take a faint wash of its colour (9% and 7%, over the neutral grey; the old fill was 10%), so on cara the Noun row reads as open and Adjective as closed.
A lone group's sub-rows: the active one is washed, or all of them when the whole group is selected.
Translation and context on one line are joined by a muted ' · ' (quanto: 'how · to what degree'; daqui: 'of · in relation to'). Stacked rows need none.

entries.summary: Function-word backs: pattern rows in the content-card style, active row outlined in its partner's colour
detail: Each pattern is an outlined box like a sense row, meaning beneath at 18px; 'Example patterns' sits under the word in the headword's font.
The active pattern is outlined in its partner's colour instead of white: think / say + que green (verb), noun + que blue.
Partners that name a thing (place, person, thing, time, reason, role, topic, endpoint) count as nouns: em + place shows a blue pill and 'maio' turns blue in the example.
Patterns with no word-type partner (se … , …, more / less + que) use the function word's own colour.

entries.summary: Card back (trial): a grouped row's shared bracket sits on the heading line
detail: daqui: 'of (in relation to)' shows as 'of  in relation to' on one line, muted, instead of 'in relation to' on its own line looking like a sub-row you could tap.

entries.summary: Card back (trial): info icon at the active row's right edge; labels moved into the note; tappable abbreviations
detail: The 'i' sits at the right edge of the active row, vertically centred, mirroring the meter; other rows show none and reserve no space (mal, não, conta).
Labels such as 'informal' leave the row and appear in its information note; a row with labels but no note gets one (cara).
Region flags lead the translation and show on the active row only (cara's Brazil flag).
Abbreviations are tappable on the active row, with no extra styling: tapping '+ger' on passar shows 'With direct object an amount of time and gerund doing something'.

entries.summary: Card back (trial): Portuguese pass — long rows stack as translation over context, both centred
detail: A row that doesn't fit on one line becomes two centred lines, translation then context (mal: 'unfavourably' / 'in an unfavourable manner'). Rows that fit stay on one line.
The info icon is glued to the last word, so it never wraps onto its own line (mal, conta, não).
'+ com', '+ de' and register labels follow the translation, not the context (acabar, sair; cara's 'informal' is a small tag).
The word-type chevron sits at the right edge (bom no longer reads 'good ·'); só's head shows 'only, just · preceding the verb' and wraps under the pill rather than pushing the meter down.
A sub-row holding a context is muted like a context (só: 'indicates that no other action…').
In a selected group on a 4+ row card, sub-rows wrap instead of being clipped (passar).

entries.summary: Card back (trial): row text centred again, but a row that wraps reads left to right
detail: Each row's text is centred in its box (option D): vamos shows 'to be', 'let's go let's move', 'come on' centred, meter on the left.

A row too long for one line keeps its lines left-aligned inside the centred block, so it reads like a sentence rather than a centred tower (não's 'not; don't; haven't negates the meaning of the verb or adverb').
Group headings and sub-rows are centred the same way (cosa: object / thing, something, anything).

entries.summary: Card back (trial): one text size for translations and contexts (20px); sub-rows are full-height tap targets
detail: Translation and context are now the same size, 20px; the translation is bold, the context regular and muted (vamos: 'let's go let's move').
Each sub-row in a group (dejar: to put, to forget, to bequeath) is at least 40px tall, left-aligned, at the same 20px size.

entries.summary: Card back (trial): rows all one size; no more outline on every sub-sense; translation no longer slides under the meter
detail: Every row's main line is the same size (19px bold) and every row is at least 44px tall, whether it is a translation (to let, still) or a context standing in for one; context after a translation is 15px and muted (it was 12px).

Opening a card whose only word type is one group (ir: to go / indicates movement, to attend) no longer outlines every sub-sense. If the card has other word types, one outline goes round that group's rows instead.
Fixed: on cards with four or more rows, switching away from a group (vamos: choose 'to be') pushed 'to go' left under the commonness meter.

entries.summary: Card back (trial): context stays beside its translation; a word type drawn as one group lifts its shared words too
detail: Inactive rows no longer push the context onto a second line under the translation, which left blank space beside the word: cosa's second row is now 'thing  concern' on one line.
On cards with four or more rows, an inactive row is one line ending in '…'; the active row still shows everything.

When a word type is one grouped row, its shared words go up to the word-type row and each sub-sense becomes its own row: aún shows 'Adverb  time' over 'still' and 'yet'; así shows 'Adverb  in a certain way' over its four translations.
When the whole group is selected (examples from every sub-sense), all of those rows are outlined.
A shared context over several translations (cosa: object over thing, something, anything) is now muted, not bold.
